basic_identification.full_title: Wooden Flush Door Shutters (Cellular, Hollow and Tubular Core Type) — Specification, Part 2: Particle Board, High Density Fibre Board, Medium Density Fibre Board and Fibre Hardboard Face Panels (Fourth Revision)
basic_identification.sector_category: Civil Engineering / Doors, Windows and Shutters (approved by the Civil Engineering Division Council and finalized by the Doors, Windows and Shutters Sectional Committee of the Bureau of Indian Standards)

sectional_committee.name: Doors, Windows and Shutters Sectional Committee

scope.summary: This standard specifies the requirements, construction, dimensions, tolerances, and testing schedules for wooden flush door shutters of the cellular, hollow, and tubular core type, fitted with face panels made of particle board, high density fibre board (HDF), medium density fibre board (MDF), or fibre hardboard. It is applicable for both decorative and non-decorative interior door shutters.

amendment_slips.description: Inserts two critical scope notes establishing that the standard formally covers hollow core flush door shutters fitted with paper and/or metal honeycomb panels in between the stiles and rails, and clarifies that the requirements of this specification are in addition or alternate to those in IS 2191 (Part 1) [1].

certification_and_marking.certification_status: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Plywood and Wooden Flush Door Shutters (Quality Control) Order' (QCO) issued by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India, all cellular, hollow, and tubular core wooden flush doors fitted with particle board, MDF, HDF, or fibre hardboard face panels must carry the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Manufacturing, importing, distributing, or selling uncertified door shutters is a statutory offense. MSMEs are granted phased transition periods, and export shipments are exempt. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to wooden doors.

requirements.detail: Every door shutter must carry the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) marked legibly and indelibly on any of its edges, accompanied by the manufacturer's registered licence number (CM/L) and standard designation (IS 2191 Part 2).
The door shutters are classified into two grades based on adhesive bonding and moisture resistance: a) BWP (Boiling Water Proof); b) MR (Moisture Resistant).
The doors are categorized into Cellular (Decorative [CD] or Non-decorative [CN]), Hollow (Decorative [HD] or Non-decorative [HN]), and Tubular (Decorative [TD] or Non-decorative [TN]) core types.
Under Amendment No. 1, hollow core door shutters are explicitly permitted to utilize paper and/or metal honeycomb panels positioned in between the stiles and rails [1].
The particle board, MDF, or HDF core board must show high resistance to moisture absorption: thickness swelling after 2 hours of water immersion must not exceed a maximum of 5 percent.
For face panels with decorative finishes of PVC foils, other type of foils, or ABS sheets, they must pass 1H of the pencil hardness test as per Annex C to IS 17637.

The face panel (formed by gluing under press processes) must satisfy minimum thicknesses: a) minimum 3 mm in the case of cellular or tubular core doors; b) minimum 6 mm in the case of hollow core doors.

The door stiles and rails must resist screw pullout during hinge installation: the load required to completely withdraw a wood screw must be at least 1 000 N, showing zero localized delamination or chipping.

To satisfy certification, doors must pass a rigorous multi-stage physical testing sequence under IS 4020, including dimensions, squareness, general flatness, local planeness, slamming resistance, end immersion, glue adhesion, and knife tests.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 2191 (Part 2) : 2022 is the mandatory national Indian Standard specification governing wooden flush door shutters of the cellular, hollow, and tubular core types that utilize particle board, HDF, MDF, or fibre hardboard face panels. Formulated under India's statutory Plywood and Wooden Flush Door Shutters Quality Control Order (QCO), all such lightweight interior door shutters must be certified by the Bureau of Indian Standards and bear the Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Amendment No. 1 (August 2024) expands the standard's scope to explicitly include paper and metal honeycomb cores in hollow core variants, establishes a strict 5% water-swelling limit for core materials, and mandates a 1H pencil hardness for PVC/ABS-foiled face finishes. It ensures that lightweight doors supplied for residential, commercial, and institutional projects meet high dimensional, moisture-resistant, and structural performance thresholds.
